`dbparser` reads public drug and gene databases from the files you download
and returns each one as a `dvobject`: a list of tables (tibbles) with a
record of where the data came from. This vignette parses two of the small
example files that ship with the package. It needs no internet connection.

```{r}
library(dbparser)
```

## A DrugBank record

DrugBank is distributed as one large XML file, which you download from
DrugBank under your own account and licence. The package includes a single
drug record in the same format.

```{r}
drugbank <- parseDrugBank(
  system.file("extdata", "drugbank_record_biotech.xml", package = "dbparser"))
```

`show_dvobject_metadata()` lists the tables in the object and their sizes:

```{r}
show_dvobject_metadata(drugbank)
```

Every parser also records where its data came from. `get_source_metadata()`
returns that record as a tibble, one row per source:

```{r}
metadata <- get_source_metadata(drugbank)
fields   <- c("source", "release", "release_date", "source_url",
              "licence_url", "parser")
data.frame(field = fields,
           value = vapply(fields, function(f) as.character(metadata[[f]]), ""),
           row.names = NULL)
```

The citation DrugBank requires is in `attribution`:

```{r}
cat(strwrap(metadata$attribution), sep = "\n")
```

`files` holds each input file with its SHA-256 hash (on R 4.5.0 or later), so
you can tell later which download a result came from:

```{r}
metadata$files[[1]]
```

## The HGNC gene nomenclature

`parseHGNC()` reads the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee's complete set and
its list of withdrawn entries. The example files hold 24 genes and 7
withdrawn entries.

```{r}
hgnc_dir <- system.file("extdata", "hgnc", package = "dbparser")
hgnc <- parseHGNC(file.path(hgnc_dir, "hgnc_complete_set.txt"),
                  withdrawn_path = file.path(hgnc_dir, "withdrawn.txt"),
                  release        = "2026-10",
                  retrieved_at   = "2026-10-16")

sapply(hgnc, dim)
```

`gene_name` has one row per symbol or name of a gene, so a name that belongs
to several genes is easy to spot. "PD1" is an alias of three genes:

```{r}
pd1   <- hgnc$gene_name[hgnc$gene_name$name == "PD1", ]
genes <- hgnc$gene[, c("hgnc_id", "symbol", "name")]
names(genes)[3] <- "approved_name"
merge(pd1, genes, by = "hgnc_id")
```

`withdrawn` shows where a withdrawn symbol went; an entry that was split has
one row per target:

```{r}
hgnc$withdrawn[hgnc$withdrawn$withdrawn_symbol == "CBBM",
               c("hgnc_id", "withdrawn_symbol", "merged_into_symbol")]
```

The source record has the same columns for every parser. Here it carries the
release and download date passed to `parseHGNC()`, HGNC's CC0 licence and the
citation HGNC asks for:

```{r}
hgnc_metadata <- get_source_metadata(hgnc)
fields        <- c("source", "release", "retrieved_at", "licence",
                   "licence_url")
data.frame(field = fields,
           value = vapply(fields,
                          function(f) as.character(hgnc_metadata[[f]]), ""),
           row.names = NULL)
cat(strwrap(hgnc_metadata$attribution), sep = "\n")
hgnc_metadata$files[[1]]
```

## More

The other parsers follow the same pattern: `parseOnSIDES()`,
`parseTWOSIDES()`, `parseHPO()`, `parseHealthCanadaDPD()` and
`parseOpenFDA()`. The worked
examples with charts are on the package website:

- [Unlocking DrugBank: parsing and visualizing mechanistic data](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/dbparser.html)
- [Integrated pharmacovigilance: linking DrugBank, OnSIDES and TWOSIDES](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/drugbank_nside.html)
- [Anticipating on-target drug effects with HPO gene-phenotype data](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/hpo_target_phenotypes.html)
